display_name: National Insurance Law ss 66-68: the child allowance (the right to it, the count of children, the amount), with s 65 and s 1 paragraph (2) of the basic amount as they need

run.method: one agent, one session, no sub-agents, from BRIEF.md

language.note: Identifiers and comments are English (@lang en). Hebrew from the Law is quoted only in `-- src:N |` comments generated mechanically from line N of the deposited source, and in short runs checked to occur verbatim in it. Hebrew from other sources (the National Insurance Institute's pages, the 5776 amending Law) is on lines tagged `-- ext:[TAG] |`, checked as NOTES.md section 7 describes.

scope: Encoded: s 66; s 67(a), (b) (both limbs, with four named refusals for the shapes of family the text does not answer); s 68(a), (b)(2), (b)(3), (c); s 65(a) 'insured' and 'child' and s 65(b) as far as ss 66-68 need them; s 1 'child' and s 1 'the basic amount' paragraph (2)(a)-(c) as far as s 65 and s 68 need them. Inert: s 65(a)'s note on regulations, s 68(b)(1) (deleted), s 68(d)-(יא) (repealed), s 1 'the Institute' and 'the Administration'. Out of scope: s 1's updating clause and the other limbs of 'the basic amount' (row IL-04's s 1); s 69; s 69A and s 71 (both declined by name where a case reaches them); s 72; s 238; s 381 and the rounding regulations; the Income Tax Ordinance s 121B (row IL-03), the Income Support Law and the Maintenance (Assurance of Payment) Law, whose results are inputs. Days from 1 May 2015; the basic amounts in force are an input, and the National Insurance Institute's published table for 1 May 2015 to 31 December 2026 is a separate module marked not-law. Amounts are before rounding. See NOTES.md sections 1-3. Version 0.2.0 adds a second question, for a family in a month: the same answer for the children the caller says s 72 pays for in the month (s 72 is still not encoded; its answer is an input), with s 65's age limb met for the month by a child whose 18th birthday is on or after the month's first day and who is born by its last (NOTES.md, 'Version 0.2.0', 06-S72; fork F19).

period_answered.text: days from 1 May 2015 (Economic Efficiency Law 5776-2015 s 29(a)); earlier days declined by name
period_answered.published_figures: 1 May 2015 to 31 December 2026; from 1 January 2027 declined by name wherever an amount is needed (0.2.0, 06-W1: a family with no child in any count needs no figure and is answered)
period_answered.month_question: months from May 2015, by the month's first day (0.2.0); January 2027 on declined wherever an amount is needed

forks.F1: s 65 'his child' carries s 1's extension (stepchild, adopted child) and exclusion (married boy or girl).
forks.F2: Where the calendar has no corresponding day (29 February; three months from the 30th or 31st), dates clamp to the end of the shorter month. (0.2.0, DATE; waits on Meng, BACKLOG IL-24) Readings: (i) clamp, held by this row and by rows IL-05 (F19) and IL-08 NII half (N4); (ii) roll to the 1st of the next month, held by no row or tester; (iii) refuse, held by this row's independent tester (finding 2) and IL-08's (D-46 to D-48). (i) stays the default until a ruling; the tests resting on it are labelled.
forks.F3: s 65(b): an absence not yet ended is measured from the day of leaving to the day asked about. (0.2.0, 06-F5) A return day before the day asked about is not 'past' in this sense: such an absence is not in progress and is reported as a problem with the facts. The return day itself is a day of the absence (assumed, not ruled).
forks.F4: The count is ordered by date of birth, eldest first; children born the same day keep the family list's order.
forks.F5: s 66: which tax year's additional-tax liability governs is not decided; the input is the caller's answer for the day. (0.2.0, 06-W3) The capstone, row IL-07, joins it to row IL-03's s 121B for the tax year in which the month falls (its fork K5, RECONCILE.md N12); this row's F5 stays open.
forks.F6: An insured father excluded by s 66 keeps the children in his count ('the insured father'); no allowance is paid for them.
forks.F7: With one insured parent, the child is in that parent's count wherever the child is. (0.2.0, 06-W2) Reading (ii) is held by the independent tester (finding 1, as a refusal) and by Axiom's RuleSpec (as 'not counted', extended to a sole parent: NOTES.md Comparison, D1-D3).
forks.F8: s 67(b) first limb: the child's own parents (natural or adoptive); second limb: a natural parent and a step-parent or a proven supporter.
forks.F9: s 67(b) second limb, child with both or neither: declined. (0.2.0, 06-W2) Axiom's RuleSpec counts the child with both, or with neither (D4, D5).
forks.F10: Two insured parents both fathers or both mothers: declined (the Institute's same-sex practice noted, not encoded). (0.2.0, 06-W2) Axiom's RuleSpec: two mothers, no count; two fathers, both counts (D6).
forks.F11: Three or more insured parents, or two that fit neither limb: declined. (0.2.0, 06-W2) Axiom's RuleSpec: 'not counted' (D7).
forks.F12: 'with the mother only' means with her and not with the father.
forks.F13: s 69A 'נשים' read as women, for the refusal gate only.
forks.F14: s 68(c): the parent paid Income Support or maintenance must be the parent in whose count the children are.
forks.F15: s 65 'child' (2): the supporter must be insured.
forks.F16: s 65 'insured' (2): the absence limb is one input, the authorised employee's determination.
forks.F17: s 68(c) 'three or more children': the children in the parent's count, s 68(b) children included.
forks.F18: (0.2.0, 06-HW; waits on Meng, BACKLOG IL-24) s 65(a) 'insured' limb (2), line 803: a resident s 238 housewife not insured under Chapter 11 is (A) excluded from both limbs (taken, the encoder; nii-s65-interpretation.l4:40-44) or (B) insured under limb (2) (the independent tester, finding 4). (A) stays the default until a ruling; the encoder's tests resting on it are labelled (nii-il06-tests.l4:379, 415, 444, 465).
forks.F19: (0.2.0, 06-S72; assumed, not ruled) In a month s 72 pays for a child in the month of its 18th birthday or of a birth by the 15th, the child is in the parent's count for the month at its place by date of birth, and counts for s 68(c)'s 'three or more children'. The alternative: s 72 continues that child's payment at its former amount and the others are counted without it.

repairs.summary: v0.2.0. 06-F5: a finished absence is reported as a problem with the facts (new constructor), not read as the child's absence on the day; one answer moves (the tester's X2, from total 0 to a rejected fact). 06-S72: a second question, for a family in a month (new record `A family in a month`), for the children the caller says s 72 pays for, so an 18th birthday on the 1st is paid for its month. It is not a second composition: the rules of ss 65-68 that take a family on a day are asked a question (new enumeration `The question asked of a family on a day`), only s 65's age limb and the check on births consult it, and the day's forms are wrappers keeping their names and types; the month's forms sit beside them in s 65, s 67, s 68 and family-on-a-day (entry point `the child allowance of each person for the month, for the children section 72 pays for, at the basic amounts the Institute published for the month, in …`). Two new constructors for a listed child s 72 cannot pay for; fork F19. Forks F18 (06-HW) and the DATE readings of F2 recorded, defaults kept, tests labelled. CHK-06: check.sh declares the tester's five remaining failures and gains expected_refused. 06-W1, 06-W2, 06-W3: NOTES wording. 39 assertions added, none changed. 02-N3 and 03-N4: IL-06 keeps its names, by the lead's ruling; IL-02 and IL-03 rename theirs (NOTES.md, 'Version 0.2.0').
